decisions: Offline hierarchical bulk remains explicitly selected; ordinary incremental construction keeps its strategy.
Fused identity/source ingestion and preassigned parent IDs stay enabled for eligible offline imports.
Optional compact ordinal routing stays off: discovery reduced I/O without an elapsed-time improvement.
Unconditional projection consolidation is rejected: it adds a full rewrite, slows publication, and increases RSS on the 10M fixture.
Admitted snapshots stream directly. A 1024-run ceiling and one pre-authority staging-allocation retry select bounded consolidation only when needed.
Private source handoff checkpoints the durable recovery manifest and uses zero obsolete-file grace while preserving reader/checkpoint pins, releasing superseded ingest generations before clustering.
Private source/projection SSTs cap entries at65536; writers cap initial reservation by the configured output limit. This bounds per-file indexes while lazy concatenation bounds live logical streams.
The matched entry-cap phase experiment reduces consolidation allocator peak from208.8MB to47.6MB without observed latency regression; variable process RSS is not a claimed improvement.
A hard allocator quota differs from the 16MiB cache retention target and whole-process RSS; report all separately.
Current 1M import qualifies the reviewed runtime; earlier version-bound repetitions provide performance observations; the earlier one-control comparison is observational, not three alternating pairs.
Source-backed Parquet reranking, a direct final-format emitter and subtree-frontier recovery are not claimed as implemented.
measurement_limitations: Shared workstation, local filesystem framed object store; not remote-provider throughput guarantees.
Operation timings include source preparation, identity, receipts, clustering and artifact candidate, but exclude final external metadata CAS and reopened recall.
Phase timings are nested and cannot be summed as disjoint costs.
The first v48 control completed but the old harness rejected a soft cache-target overage and discarded process counters. Recovered CPU, RSS and whole-process wall remain null.
Historical discovery CPU and I/O effects do not substitute for a matched current-runtime comparison.
Artifact candidates, reopen and recall are checked; full production deployment and real S3 fault injection remain separate from this fixture.
